title: Karnaugh maps 2: simplify to gates
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: In a Karnaugh-map pair, A stays 0 and B changes between 0 and 1. What is the simplified term?
options: This result cannot be obtained using the stated method.
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: ¬A Explanation: A stays 0, so retain NOT A (¬A). B changes, so remove B.

questions.prompt: Show the array after one complete left-to-right pass of ascending bubble sort on [8, 3, 6, 2].
questions.feedback: Model answer: [3, 6, 2, 8] Explanation: Swap 8 and 3 → [3, 8, 6, 2]; swap 8 and 6 → [3, 6, 8, 2]; swap 8 and 2 → [3, 6, 2, 8]. The largest value is now last.

questions.prompt: C#: int[,,] scores = new int[2, 3, 4]; How many values can it store? What does scores.GetLength(2) return?
questions.feedback: Model answer: 24 values; GetLength(2) = 4 Explanation: 2 layers × 3 rows × 4 columns = 24 values. Dimension 2 is the third dimension (columns).

questions.prompt: Add 01000000 0011 and 01000000 0010. Format: 8-bit two’s-complement fractional mantissa + 4-bit two’s-complement exponent. Show exponent alignment and the final normalised result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: 01100000 0011 (denary 6) Explanation: Align to exponent 3 by shifting the second mantissa right: 01000000 → 00100000. Add the mantissas: 01000000 + 00100000 = 01100000. The exponent remains 0011. This is normalised: 0.75 × 2³ = 6.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: efficient group — A group of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 neighbouring 1s.
overlap — The same 1 can appear in two different groups.
wraparound — The left/right edges touch, and the top/bottom edges touch.
literal — An input letter, such as A, or its NOT, ¬A.
product term — An expression made with AND, such as A ∧ B.
simplified expression — The same output with fewer variables or gate inputs.

blocks.title: Find the 1s
blocks.text: Look at the 2×2 map on the left. Three squares contain 1. We need to cover them in groups of neighbouring 1s. Use rectangles containing 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 cells. Include only 1s, and choose the largest useful groups. Diagonal cells are not neighbours.

blocks.title: A square may belong to two groups
blocks.text: This is overlap. It is allowed when it makes the expression simpler.

blocks.title: Keep the inputs that stay the same
blocks.text: Bottom pair: A stays 1; B changes. Keep A. Right pair: B stays 1; A changes. Keep B.

blocks.title: The outside columns form one group
blocks.text: BC runs 00, 01, 11, 10. The first and last columns are neighbours: only B changes between 00 and 10. Imagine rolling the map so its left and right edges meet. The four 1s make a 2 × 2 group; the middle 0s are outside it.

blocks.title: Worked example · How do two groups become a circuit?
blocks.text: Rows A; columns BC in Gray-code order.
